Adversarial content hides in workspace skill files, emails and web pages. Across 2520 sandboxed trials with five language models as agent backbones, attack success rates run from 40 to 75 percent. Rates vary sharply by vector, with skill instructions most dangerous. The strongest model blocks credential forwarding and destructive actions. Safety depends on the full deployment stack, not the backbone alone.
arxiv-2604-01738: Qiao and colleagues present AeroTherm-GPT, a model agent for hypersonic thermal protection design, where generated artifacts often break cascading constraints. General models miss the multi-gate rules of safety-critical work. Their closed-loop framework runs generation, validation, graph-guided repair, execution and audit. A dependency graph maps how constraint types resolve, steering repairs to upstream faults first, so one fix clears several violations. On HyTPS-Bench it reaches an 88.7 percent overall success rate, beating its ablation baseline.
arxiv-2604-01838: Stein and colleagues use an agent-based model to test whether free information exchange helps groups hold correct beliefs. Modern networks, such as social media platforms, assume users should face no limits on freely exchanging information about a topic. Yet even among truth-seeking, cooperative agents with processing, unconstrained exchange can harm group belief correctness. If it can harm such idealized agents, it can plausibly harm real users too. The authors argue that limits on information flow deserve thought in designing networks with societal impact.
arxiv-2604-02338: Kowsher and colleagues propose LiME, a lightweight mixture of experts for multimodal tasks. MoE-PEFT methods need one adapter per expert, so parameters scale with expert count. LiME instead uses one shared PEFT module modulated by expert vectors, cutting parameters and fitting any PEFT method. Zero parameter routing uses frozen representations, with no learned router. Theory proves more experts preserve more task information and modulation nears full PEFT with bounded error. Tests on a 47 task benchmark show strong performance with 4 times fewer parameters and 29 percent faster training.
arxiv-2604-02838: Mitra and Sommer model how RNA polymerase clusters and the chromosome organize in space inside E. coli cells. Ribosomal RNA operons rank among the most active transcription sites, and binding there forms dense clusters that pull operons together. Liquid-liquid phase separation is the suspected driver, with NusA playing a key role. Their simulations propose that NusA proteins attract each other, showing a miscibility gap at higher levels, driving condensate formation through a polymer-assisted pathway, reconciling imaging and Hi-C observations.
arxiv-2604-03238: Ghafouri and colleagues argue that reinforcement learning from human feedback rests on a shaky premise: annotator responses often are not genuine preferences at all. People may answer without opinions, build preferences on the spot, or read the same question differently, and these flaws bite hardest on value judgments. Filtering inconsistent annotators flipped harm verdicts for about 19 percent of prompts, showing the field often models noise as signal.
arxiv-2604-03538: Betancourt and Machta show that thermal jitter sets basic limits on ion channel function. Two noise sources matter: shot noise from discrete bits of ionic charge and Johnson-Nyquist noise from thermal field jitter. For a single channel, shot noise rules and caps voltage sensing sharpness at about 10 mV on 10 µs timescales. When many channels pool, Johnson-Nyquist noise beats shot noise and bounds total sensed information, with the switch at counts within measured ranges.
arxiv-2604-03638: Jorge Betancor, Marta de León-Contreras, and Lourdes Rodríguez-Mesa defined logarithmic versions of two operators. One belongs to Schrödinger operators with a suitable potential; the other is the discrete Laplacian on integers. The work covers both the smooth setting and the discrete setting in one account. Both versions act nonlocally, so the authors built them through extension problems like those used for fractional Laplacians. Here the logarithm shows up as a boundary value, reached by a more involved route.
arxiv-2604-03938: Kwon Ko and Hyoungwook Jin asked what an agentic society of everyday objects would need to coordinate well. Thirty years after Wooldridge and Jennings defined agents by autonomy, reactivity, pro-activeness, and social ability, smart objects can now act as agents together. A scenario of a bullied teenager showed both promise and failure modes: false positives that break trust, deadlocks that block action, and adversarial corruption. The open questions split into sharing choices, judgment calls, and timing of action.
arxiv-2604-04038: WooJoo Kim and colleagues built FLAME, a framework that condenses ensemble diversity into a single network for sequential recommendation. Training many networks from scratch costs heavily and wobbles under noisy mutual supervision. FLAME simulates exponential diversity with just two networks via modular ensemble, freezing one as a semantic anchor and aligning the other through guided mutual learning. At inference only the learnable network runs, matching group performance with zero overhead, and tests on six datasets showed faster convergence and higher NDCG.
arxiv-2604-04338: Srivastava uses Kolmogorov n-widths to benchmark reduced-order methods for phononic, acoustic and photonic bands. Bloch operators are holomorphic in the wave vector, so eigenpairs inherit that holomorphy where the spectral gap stays positive. The n-width of the manifold decays fast, at a rate set by the smallest neighbouring gap. For band clusters, spectral projectors make internal crossings moot; only the outer gap matters. These results bound any linear reduction method's error sharply, and tests confirm fast decay with a greedy algorithm nearing optimal convergence.
arxiv-2604-04738: Shang, Yu and Chen define fine-tuning integrity, a way to check that a released model differs from its base only in a class of updates. Their succinct difference proofs use zero-knowledge methods to certify norm-bounded, low-rank, and sparse drift without showing model weights. Proof size and check cost hinge on update shape, not weight count, and they prove soundness, zero-knowledge, and succinctness  with a lower bound making assumptions necessary. Tests on synthetic cases and GPT-2 fine-tuning show compact proofs and fast checks.
arxiv-2604-04938: Torres Alegre and Mora Jimenez study metacognition, the monitoring and control of one's own thinking, as a sequence of state-changing judgments. An agent assesses an inner state, updates it, and may judge again under changed criteria, so order effects are common. The authors build an operational framework that separates the back-action of judging from the observed output. They show order dependence rules out any faithful Boolean-commutative representation. They then ask the stronger question of whether observed order effects can always be explained in classical terms.
arxiv-2604-05038: Toga and four co-authors study information spread in Rydberg arrays through analog out-of-time-order correlator math. Such tools probe quantum chaos and scrambling, but tests on analog quantum computers are hard because old methods require backward time flow. The authors develop a randomized protocol and run it on Aquila by QuEra. Their approach uses global randomized quenches that mimic the unitary 2-design traits needed to extract infinite-temperature correlators from statistical links. They show the protocol by seeing the lightcone of information spread in 1D Rydberg arrays.
arxiv-2604-05238: Ramos, de Queiroz, and de Oliveira present Lean 4 work on Nagata's factoriality theorem. If R is a domain and S has S-inverse-R a UFD, then R is a UFD. The hypothesis, that every element of S is a finite product of primes in S, replaces a condition. It is packaged for Localization S and through IsLocalization formulations. They formalize two proofs that polynomial rings over UFDs are UFDs: via localization at powers of X and at primes to fractions. They also obtain the corollary for two variables.
arxiv-2604-05538: Mohanty and Mahapatra build a fresh set of Ricci-flat black-hole and soliton solutions carrying primary scalar hair in anti-de Sitter space. The scalar field and curvature stay regular throughout, and the hairy soliton forms the ground state. A first-order phase transition links black hole and soliton, with the soliton's favored temperature window widening as hair grows.
arxiv-2604-06238: Shvets proves a supercongruence for symmetric-cube coefficients: for primes from 5 upward, every m, coefficients at mp and m agree modulo fourth powers of p. The proof uses three ingredients. First, a modular identification of the function with eta powers, whose logarithmic derivative is a weight-5 Eisenstein series. Second, congruences for those coefficients plus a Lagrange-Bürmann extraction. Third, a Hecke descent on weakly holomorphic forms, with a 2D defect space and the second cusp via Fricke involution. The Mao-Tian recurrence also drops an order.
arxiv-2604-06338: Satharasi and four colleagues develop an SP-ICL update law for uncertain nonlinear control-affine systems with linear parameters. Unknown parameters are learned with l1 regularization, a common tool in system ID and machine learning. Unlike existing approaches, their online update law merges the regularization penalty with concurrent learning via sliding modes. Lyapunov analysis shows closed-loop paths stay bounded under the new update law. Simulations verify the sparsity penalty recovers sparse dynamics during tracking.
arxiv-2604-06438: Katz frames retraining as a cost-touchy regret decision. Deployed systems use fixed dates, though age varies. The watch state is posterior learning debt, the gap from shadow to frozen beliefs. Refresh cost is set against expected regret of waiting. A continuous version retrains when expected regret exceeds cost. A proof-of-concept tests it. An age-tuned debt-threshold policy beats dates refresh in all 72 cells and CUSUM in 58. Debt-utility and hybrid-utility policies beat refresh. The contribution is a transparent layer, not a drift detection swap.
arxiv-2604-06538: van Dam, Koolen, and Xiong build non-amorphic schemes. A scheme is amorphic when every fusion yields another scheme. Earlier work: a scheme with at most one off-type relation must be amorphic. They now build non-amorphic schemes of four or more classes with precisely two relations outside the Latin square and negative Latin square types. They ask whether different strongly regular graph types can coexist in one scheme. When one relation is a lattice graph, every other strongly regular relation must be of Latin square type.
arxiv-2604-06638: Zhang and five colleagues design RPM-Net, a network for spotting unknown threats amid many uneven attack classes. For each known attack type it learns a reciprocal point, a stand-in for what the class is not, and adds margin rules that give unknown-threat calls a geometric reading. A stronger variant, RPM-Net++, adds Fisher discriminant regularization. Tests show it beats existing methods on F1-score, AUROC, and AUPR-OUT, with code released for practical use.
arxiv-2604-06938: Won and four colleagues tune ISP pipelines at the sequence level with POS-ISP. Prior work tunes chains from preset modules, yet joint tuning of module order and settings stays hard. Neural architecture search suffers a train-test mismatch, while step-wise reward learning trains shakily at high compute cost. POS-ISP frames pipeline tuning as one global order guess. It guesses module order and settings in one forward pass, tuning on a final task reward with no mid-step supervision or repeat runs. Tests show better results more cheaply.
arxiv-2604-07038: Miki and six colleagues test joint body sense with a robotic joint. Joint sensors were seen as limit alarms giving place only at extreme angles, while muscle spindles were the angle sensors. The team copied slow-long Type I joint receptors and gauged promise with a life-like joint. Type I-like sensors alone sensed with error under 2 degrees in bending and twisting. Joint receptors matter more than known, with spindle and sensor weights shifting during growth and change.
arxiv-2604-07238: Li and three colleagues measure the price of privacy in language identification and generation under differential privacy. For approximate privacy with a fixed privacy budget, the private error rates match the non-private ones: exponentially small in sample size for both tasks. Under pure privacy, the exponents shrink by a factor equal to the smaller of one and the privacy budget, and the authors show this factor is tight. The cost of privacy is therefore mild: absent under approximate privacy, and exactly that factor under pure privacy.
arxiv-2604-07738: Adelman, Olivares-Nadal, and Xie optimize how a scarce treatment with wide benefits should be allocated. Health management must juggle varied patient traits, how those traits evolve and respond over time, and people entering and leaving the group. Their approach uses measurized Markov models that fold all three pieces together. The model optimizes the long-term makeup of the patient group under capacity limits. That framing sidesteps tracking every person's traits while keeping allocation doable and within ethical bounds.
arxiv-2604-08138: Gogawale and five colleagues propose Bag of Bags for Genizah join retrieval. A join is a set of fragments originally from one manuscript. Given a query fragment, the task is retrieving sibling fragments. Bag of Bags replaces the global codebook of classical Bag of Words with a fragment vocabulary of local words. The pipeline uses a sparse convolutional autoencoder on binarized pieces, encodes page components, clusters embeddings by per-image k-means, and compares images by distances between local vocabularies. The best variant, Chamfer, reaches Hit@1 of 0.78 with strong MRR.
arxiv-2604-08338: GhoshDastider, Pal, and Mishra present a random mean-reverting jump-diffusion model for rainfall series, checked with long-term half-hourly rainfall data from North-East India. The model captures intermittent and extreme-event rainfall dynamics, reproducing superdiffusive behavior with exponent around 1.8, plus seen probability distributions and multifractal traits. By varying key settings, they show Log-Normal to Gamma transitions and control over extreme events and dry-patch spans. Spectral and wavelet checks confirm the simulated series matches dominant scales in real rainfall data.
arxiv-2604-08538: Zhang and six colleagues build ParseBench, a document parsing benchmark judged by what AI agents actually need: correct tables, exact chart data, faithful content, meaningful formatting, and visual grounding. Its roughly 2,000 human checked enterprise pages span insurance, finance, and government across five skill dimensions. No method among 14 tested leads on all five, with LlamaParse Agentic best overall at 84.9 percent.
arxiv-2604-08738: Maalaoui and Martino study a conformally invariant Dirac type equation on closed spin shapes of dimension at least four. They show the Aubin type bound for the problem is always strict unless the shape is a stretched round sphere. The result gives a proof for a ground state of the Dirac-Einstein problem in dimension four, the first general result outside small change or special cases.
arxiv-2604-08938: Moffat and Hawking tackle a teaching problem in data structures and algorithms courses: how to make students feel why efficient methods matter. They present two plain problems, each with a chain of improvements to a basic method, so runtimes fall from days or even years to a few seconds. Calling such chains thrills of algorithms, they argue that the dramatic drop lands viscerally in a way lectures rarely match. They frame the demonstrations as classroom material for motivating algorithm design.
arxiv-2604-09438: Ram, Sommer, Schmitz, and Steimle introduce Intent Lenses for turning opportunistic photos into structured visual notes. Quick photos of slides, exhibits, or artifacts preserve information but rarely become meaningful notes. Existing automatic note generation often yields generic summaries missing what users meant to capture. Intent Lenses reify inferred capture-time intent into reusable objects encoding function, sources, and detail level. Built with large language models for academic conference photos on a spatial canvas, the system was tested with nine academics, whose notes matched expectations and aided deeper sensemaking.
arxiv-2604-09538: Mahmud and four colleagues build an explicit quantum block encoding for the Difference-of-Gaussian operator on a periodic grid. Their key move splits the operator into two normalized Gaussian distributions. Each is prepared by direct circuits, with the minus sign carried by a single Pauli-Z gate. The encoding then maps onto the Linear Combination of Unitaries framework, with no signed amplitude loading or memory oracles. Its subnormalization factor stays fixed at 2 for any grid size, dimension, or stencil width.
arxiv-2604-09638: Fang, Garcia Bernardo, and van Kesteren offer a step-by-step guide to using large language models for text annotation in social-science and humanities research. Many researchers struggle to adopt the models, handle their limits, and produce reproducible workflows. Annotation errors can bias statistics despite high apparent accuracy. The guide covers how the models work, setting up projects, prompting and evaluating without overfitting, and folding annotations into statistical analysis while accounting for error. Python and R examples run throughout, with cost and reproducibility in view.
arxiv-2604-09838: Phan and three co-authors present a diffusion-based framework for making 2D vector fields from sparse, matching streamline inputs while keeping realism. The method uses a guided denoising diffusion model with free guidance, growing fields step by step that preserve shape and physical constraints. Experiments show it makes plausible vector fields following physical laws while staying faithful to sparse inputs, outperforming older tuning-based approaches in freedom and physical fit.
arxiv-2604-09938: Yilmaz builds a unified setup for farm rigs, tying gears, energy, draft, shape, costs, carbon, and chance onto one code path, and applies it to CableTract. CableTract pairs a winch unit with a lighter anchor module held by screw piles, pulling a cable across a strip for a light tool carriage. Heavy bodies stay on the headland; the carriage alone enters, running a 10-tool library for cables. The setup chains cable, drive, draft, energy, cover, packing, costs, and response models, yielding energy and packing gains and off-grid use.
arxiv-2604-11038: Peng and two colleagues present EgoFun3D, a task, dataset, and benchmark for interactive objects from egocentric videos. Such objects matter for embodied AI but are scarce, so modeling from real videos is valuable. The task targets simulation-ready interactive objects from such video. While prior work focuses on articulations, EgoFun3D captures cross-part functional mappings through function templates. A stove knob rotation controls burner temperature. Function templates enable precise evaluation and compilation into code across simulation platforms. The dataset holds 517 such videos with paired geometry and articulation annotations.
arxiv-2604-11238: Mukhopadhyay and five colleagues boost third-harmonic generation, a process that triples light frequency, in silicon nitride metasurfaces. Two flat designs favor different light polarizations and trap near-infrared laser pulses at tiny scales. The trapped light converts visible light into ultraviolet and deep-ultraviolet output up to a hundred times stronger than a flat slab. The result shows a common chip-compatible material can serve short-wavelength nonlinear photonics. In short, careful shaping of a plain material beats hunting for rare new ones.
arxiv-2604-11438: Lopes Seeger and seven colleagues control Floquet magnons in a magnetic vortex. Microwave tests of vortex-state magnetic tunnel junctions show Floquet sidebands forming frequency combs whose existence depends on the vortex core orbit. Shifting the core with an applied magnetic field switches the system between regular and Floquet magnons under identical drive conditions, demonstrating hysteretic control of the Floquet spectrum. A vortex-magnon model traces the effect to multiple stable gyration radii created by Floquet-mediated feedback, making magnetic state initialization a switch.
arxiv-2604-11538: Ding and three colleagues present ResearchCube, a system for exploring research ideas across trade-off dimensions. It recasts evaluation dimensions as bipolar spectra, such as theory-driven versus data-driven, and plots ideas as points in a user-built 3D space. Users pick up to three dimension pairs as axes, then steer and combine ideas by dragging rather than prompting. A study with 11 researchers found the bipolar dimensions scaffolded thinking, the spatial view gave agency chatbots lack, and users wanted fluid moves across dimension counts.
arxiv-2604-11638: Mcheik establishes precompactness for conformal metrics with bounded Q-curvature on closed smooth Riemannian manifolds. On a manifold of dimension at least five with positive Yamabe invariant and semi-positive Q, the metrics are conformal to a given metric. They carry the standard sphere's volume and have nonnegative Q, bounded in an L^p sense for p above a quarter of n. Their first Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalue exceeds n. Such metrics form a precompact set in a Hölder topology.
arxiv-2604-11738: Tsur, Fischer, and Ruhman study reduced pair breaking from extended disorder in unconventional superconductors. Unconventional pairing should be suppressed by nonmagnetic disorder under Abrikosov-Gor'kov rules, yet metal dichalcogenides keep pairing despite resistance. Using a multiband model with spin-orbit links and an impurity potential like chalcogen gaps or adatoms, they compare spread with on-site point defects. Extended potentials reduce pair-breaking versus transport scatter, with the rate product near one-third over a range, since disorder matches gap structure. Such pairing proves more robust than standard rules.
arxiv-2604-11938: Jain, Mizgerd, and Vigoda study how fast a simple local chain samples proper colorings of a graph when colors only slightly outnumber the maximum degree. They prove optimal mixing for graphs of girth at least seven once colors exceed the degree by any fixed fraction, building on a non-Markovian coupling where updates may reach into future steps. New local uniformity results carry the argument down to constant degree.
arxiv-2604-12038: Mamo shows fixed-spin holographic double deeply virtual Compton scattering, and its limit, match the singlet conformal Wilson-kernel family of quantum chromodynamics. The open-string kernel came from Nishio and Watari. The BPST upper vertex gives the same family with a different power count, so the Mellin exponent is derived, not inserted by hand. The spin-2 split identifies closed and open branches with two partial waves. They are mixed eigenchannels rather than literal quark or gluon operators, putting deconvolution in a physical operator basis rather than arbitrary profiles.
arxiv-2604-12138: Agrawal and four colleagues argue retrieval-augmented generation wrongly assumes every query has one right answer, so systems chase factual certainty while flattening opinion. Their O-RAG tags documents with opinion metadata before indexing, and they score opinion-aware retrieval by Wasserstein distance. On seller forums and hotel reviews it cut the gap to corpus sentiment by 18 to 48 percent, and human judges preferred its responses 79.2 percent of the time.
arxiv-2604-12238: Couey argues many engineering failures are geometric, not material: changing matter delays failure, while changing shape can remove it. He introduces the Contact Distribution Score, the variance over a rolling surface of contact time, weighted by area, plus a stress-domain counterpart from Hertz pressure. A search over 45 developable rollers puts the oloid far ahead of the cylinder baseline, a 58-fold gap that carries across fatigue, thermal, and wear scores.
arxiv-2604-12338: Si-Qi Du, Guo-Zhu Song, and Hai-Rui Wei concentrate entanglement in high-dimensional quantum systems. Entanglement is the quantum link between distant particles. Their scheme works even when the system's exact state is unknown. Acting only at one receiver's site, it distills a fully entangled pair of three-level particles. Leftover partly entangled states remain useful for other tasks. A version for known states needs only linear optics.
arxiv-2604-12738: Slava Pimenov outlines a parallel theory of L-manifolds. Such manifolds appear in geometry, quantum cohomology, and singularity theory. Locally, one has two equivalent forms. One is an algebra over a cyclic operad. The other is a genus zero cohomological field theory. Pimenov starts instead from cyclic Lie-infinity algebras. The paper takes first steps toward the parallel theory and notes similarities between the pictures.
arxiv-2604-12938: JiaHao Li and six colleagues design beams that morph into chosen shapes. Slender parts bend under remote control. No general interpretable inverse design existed for a magneto-elastica. Their integral formulation makes global boundary constraints explicit. Key parameters weigh torques against elastic moments. Closed-form tapers yield wanted shapes for clamped beams. The theory matches the classical inverse elastica with no field. A stiffness-tailoring tessellation extends the design. Tests confirm the predictions.
arxiv-2604-13138: Khalil, Al-Dweik, Aloqeili, and Mahomed construct four coframes of invariant 1-forms for non-linearizable fourth-order ordinary differential equations with a 5D Lie symmetry subalgebra. Using the stepwise Cartan matching method with rank zero, they match each of four distinct branches to a coframe. The coframes define the equations under point transformation, and the authors give a recipe for finding the point map itself, shown through examples.
arxiv-2604-13238: Huang gives a quadratic form on functions over the gap poset of the number semigroup made by a and b. Used on the indicator function of an upward closed subset, the form gives exactly the Gorsky-Mazin dinv statistic of that subset, viewed as a Young subdiagram. For pairs of subdiagrams, the linked symmetric bilinear form equals a novel nonnegative cross-dinv statistic, and a bound for falling functions shows working positive firmness on the matching cone. The main theorem was checked in Lean and Mathlib by AxiomProver.
arxiv-2604-13338: Ramírez and Protas search computationally for possible singularities in three-dimensional Navier-Stokes flows on a periodic domain. The Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin conditions say a regular flow must keep certain norms bounded, so the authors solve variational optimization problems that push those norms as high as possible. They try two formulations, over Lebesgue and Sobolev spaces, with a new method for the first case. No unbounded growth appears, but the worst flows enter a regime where growth matches finite-time singularity rates before fading.
arxiv-2604-13538: Ichinose and four colleagues untangle two things mixed together in answers from large language models: facts learned during pretraining and the habit of following instructions learned later. Their method, CoDIT, contrasts a tuned model against its untuned twin while generating answers, damping shared knowledge and boosting instruction-following behavior. Models trained on the resulting data beat models trained on plain generated answers.
arxiv-2604-13638: Rousseau and five colleagues present Cerisier, a new logic for modular reasoning about attestation in capability machines. It lets an enclave prove its identity to distrusting components. Tracking how trust evolves after such proof is security-critical and hard. No prior method does this in parts. Cerisier, built with Iris logic and proved in Rocq, adds CHERI-TrEE enclave tools. It gives untrusted code a universal contract covering safety and local proof, and demos cover outsourced work, mutual proof, and a trusted sensor.
arxiv-2604-13838: Schurmann and Serov describe a further family of solutions to the cubically nonlinear Schrodinger equation. An earlier article proved some solutions cannot exist in the general case, while presenting solutions for the non-generic case. The new family enlarges the set of non-generic solutions. In plain terms, the work maps where solutions exist and where they cannot, and it widens the known territory on the existence side.
arxiv-2604-14138: Caraceni and three colleagues describe a leaf-by-leaf trimming rule that builds nested uniform binary plane trees by picking the best of three matches at each step. Though each single step matches a known coupling, the full process scales to a surprising càdlàg erasure of Brownian trees. The authors link that limit to the flavor of SLE theory.
arxiv-2604-14538: Zheng and fifteen colleagues report an odd-parity f-wave charge bond order in the kagome metal CsV3Sb5, found with scanning tunneling microscopy and photoemission spectroscopy. The phase keeps translation symmetry yet breaks inversion symmetry, opening a gap in the spectrum at a Dirac point missed before. That gap opening gives a textbook case of Gross-Neveu physics for dynamical mass generation and parity breaking. The order itself is fleeting, vanishing abruptly below 10 kelvin and hinting at a hidden electronic state that local probes cannot see.
arxiv-2604-14738: Brown, Dean, and Doshi-Velez built a framework that predicts how a stress-relief activity will shift heart rate, heart-rate variability, and beat spacing over the next 15 to 120 minutes. A Transformer model forecasts the percent change from a pre-activity baseline at several horizons, plus a call on whether each measure rises, falls, or stays flat. The study pairs wearable sensor streams with user-tagged events. As a proof of concept it shows such tailored forecasts are feasible, though larger trials and, where needed, regulatory review must come first.
arxiv-2604-14838: Civale, Semeraro, Bagdanov, and Magi challenge reading single-cell models only at the final layer. With scFoundation and Tahoe-X1, the best layer depends on task and context for trajectory inference and perturbation prediction. Trajectory inference peaks at 60 percent depth, 31 percent above final layers, while perturbation optima shift 0 to 96 percent across T-cell states. In quiescent cells, first-layer embeddings beat deeper layers. Where features are extracted matters as much as what was learned, so layer choice needs evaluation per task and cell context, not the default end.
arxiv-2604-15638: Mangan and five colleagues present contact-aware planning and control for continuum robots in tight fragile spaces such as blood vessels, where contact is often unavoidable. Their planner scores contact quality, penalizing hazardous interactions while allowing benign ones, and yields feasible trajectories plus contact-aware Jacobians for closed-loop control. Hardware trials on patient-scan anatomical models reached every target with no dangerous tip contact, at tracking errors near 1 to 2 millimeters.
arxiv-2604-15838: Hu, Gauthier, and Naima tackle drift in spatiotemporal forecasting. Both single series and links across a network change over time, so models trained on old patterns fail. Their framework, Reversible Residual Normalization, uses place-aware transforms that can run backward inside its blocks. It learns in a tidy space, then undoes the change at the end. Center scaling plus graph nets with capped spectra make the method work with any model, aiming for steady results on changing networks.
arxiv-2604-15938: Yu and four colleagues present VADF, a vision-driven framework that speeds up diffusion policies for robotic manipulation. Uniform sampling ignores sample difficulty, causing slow training and frequent inference timeouts. During training, an adaptive loss network predicts per-step difficulty in real time, guiding weighted sampling toward high-loss regions. At inference, a hierarchical vision task segmenter splits instructions into simple and complex subtasks, giving simple actions shorter noise schedules and longer execution runs. The design cuts training steps, lowers compute overhead, and raises early success rates.
arxiv-2604-16038: Bonhomme and Dulaunoy ask whether vulnerability sightings, like proof-of-concept posts or online chats, can be predicted over time. Building on VLAI, their transformer model for scores from text, they test whether scores improve time-series forecasts. SARIMAX models improve little and suit sparse, short, bursty data poorly, often yielding wide ranges and sometimes below-zero values. Count-based methods like Poisson regression give more stable, clear forecasts, mainly for weekly totals. Simpler exponential decay functions offer short-horizon estimates without long records.
arxiv-2604-16138: Nunnari, Jain, and Gebhard present a dataset and model for sentiment analysis of German sign language fairy tales. First, they analyze negative, neutral, and positive valence in fairy tale text segments using four models and majority voting, reaching inter-annotator agreement. Second, they extract face and body features from sign segments using MediaPipe. Finally, they train an XGBoost model on video features. Results show about 63 percent balanced accuracy. Analysis finds eyebrow, mouth, hip, elbow, and shoulder motion contribute, showing face and body matter equally for sentiment.
arxiv-2604-16238: Guan and 12 colleagues introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine-learning framework to improve subseasonal weather forecasts two to six weeks ahead. Skill drops sharply at that range as errors compound and biases build in the chaotic atmosphere. Applied to leading European Centre models, their method doubles the AI Forecasting System's modest subseasonal skill. It also improves the debiased dynamical model for 91 percent of pressure targets, 92 percent of temperature targets, and 98 percent of precipitation targets.
arxiv-2604-16538: Zhang and colleagues study agents that translate plain mathematics into faithful Lean 4 code. The gap between set-theory instinct and strict type theory leads models to invent fake library names. They test three tool types: expert-draft querying, symbol-name search, and build feedback through a Lean REPL. The agent beats one-shot rivals by large margins on build success and semantic match. That split then shows each tool type's extra gain to overall scores.
arxiv-2604-16638: Tyrovolas and colleagues model zero-energy tunable smart panels under stepped phase shifts. Such panels harvest energy from nearby signals, giving lean settable spaces. Energy harvest couples to signal bounce, and limited phase control tangles that link. The authors analyze energy outage risk and energy value under time switching and element splitting. Sender-side and user-side setups are studied, with rest phase error modeled by stats. Stepping affects harvest and bounce together, forcing trade-offs in phase detail and harvest-and-reflect scheme choice.
arxiv-2604-16738: Liu and colleagues examine teacher-authored prompts and starters for student-AI dialogue. The Spring 2025 pilot covered 39 classrooms, yielding 1,479 conversations with 878 unique students. Conversations matched intent, with 71 percent on-track and fewer than 1 percent off-track. A demand gap persisted, with 38 percent under-reaching the targeted level, approaching 50 percent at level three. Explicit finish lines cut that gap by zero point two two levels, and no-direct-answers guardrails cut final-answer rates by eight point five. Teacher prompts translate intent into structured dialogue, though higher-order reasoning needs support.
arxiv-2604-16938: Kulbak and four colleagues analyze magnetization dynamics in ferromagnetic nanomagnets near equilibrium. They track how the resonance frequency, damping, and quality factor depend on the curvature of the local energy minimum. Near bifurcation points, where the number of stable minima changes, they show the standard quality-factor approximation breaks down, with attention to decay times there.
arxiv-2604-17138: Behr summarizes ATLAS results on a significant excess of top-antitop events near the production threshold in LHC Run-2 data. The excess fits the formation of top-antitop quasi-bound states, first hypothesized almost 40 years ago. The contribution outlines a path toward further characterization of the excess and its quasi-bound-state interpretation.
arxiv-2604-17338: Chai and seven colleagues ask whether code-debugging models truly fix bugs or simply rewrite whole programs. Their Precise Debugging Benchmark turns any coding dataset into a debugging test by planting verified single bugs and combining them into multi-bug programs. Two new scores track how many edits were truly needed and how many bugs were actually resolved. Leading models passed over 76 percent of unit tests yet scored below 45 percent on precision, even when told to edit minimally, and fancier iterative strategies barely helped.
arxiv-2604-17538: Beker, Geist, Paulus, and Martius attack the collision-detection bottleneck in robot simulation for contact-rich tasks. Standard routines are tuned for CPU speed and small memory, but their branching logic blocks the smooth gradients and GPU vectorization that modern optimization needs. The authors design a fresh pipeline built for twice differentiability and massive parallelization, covering how contact surfaces between rigid bodies are constructed. The goal is faster, gradient-aware planning where robots touch, push, and grasp.
arxiv-2604-17638: Majhi, Mondal, and Agnihotri compare refresher training modes for community healthcare workers in India, the frontline workers for mothers and children. Classroom training proves ineffective for knowledge retention, calling for short, frequent revision. The study recruited 270 workers into three equal groups of 90: standard classroom training, a physical card game, and a smartphone game. Knowledge was tested before and after, and retention after six months. All three groups improved significantly, with pre-post gains higher in the digital mode, though six-month retention did not differ between digital and card modes.
arxiv-2604-17738: Liang and three colleagues present mira-embeddings-v1, a meaning reranking system for hiring. Talent sourcing is a two-stage pipeline aiming at recall on a budget. A search tool returns a shortlist per description, to be reranked so strong talent ranks first. The system reshapes vectors with LLM-made data and fixes edge errors with a light head. From real job posts, a five-stage flow makes good and hard bad examples. Two-round LoRA tuning follows: job-description contrast training, then description-to-CV triplet matching.
arxiv-2604-17838: Jeon and two colleagues present a unified approach for diffusion models that must stay inside nonconvex feasible sets defined by equality and inequality constraints. Instead of costly projections onto the set, a landing mechanism keeps samples feasible throughout forward and backward sampling, using both overdamped and underdamped dynamics. That motion also speeds mixing toward the prior. Tests show fewer function calls and less memory use in training and inference, with sample quality close to strong baselines.
arxiv-2604-18038: Xing and Gouliev evaluate racial bias in language models used clinically, viewing five models through the EU AI Act across synthetic case generation and diagnosis ranking. Every model departed from observed racial distributions in synthetic cases, with GPT-4.1 showing the smallest deviation, while DeepSeek V3 led diagnosis. Embedding DeepSeek V3 in an agentic workflow improved mean and median p-values and mean difference over the standalone model, though not on every metric. The findings support multi-metric bias evaluation and suggest agentic workflows may reduce some explicit bias.
arxiv-2604-18138: Josué de Araújo, Gilderlan de Araújo, and André de Almeida propose semi-blind receivers for wireless systems that combine reconfigurable intelligent surfaces with fluid antennas. Channel estimation is hard here because links shift as antenna ports and surface settings change. Their framework estimates channels and symbols together through two transmission protocols, one built on a PARAFAC tensor model and one on a nested PARAFAC2 model. Simulations show accurate recovery with far less training overhead than pilot-based methods.
arxiv-2604-18338: Loi and seven colleagues map the magnetic field of the Fornax cluster from the densest rotation-measure grid yet, 508 sources strong. Comparing the grid with simulations constrains the field's strength and structure. The field follows a power law with a central strength near 5 microgauss, fading with plasma density. A comparison across 17 clusters finds longer correlation lengths in massive merging systems, and the steep Fornax profile hints at recent central re-amplification by its radio galaxy.
arxiv-2604-18438: Zhai, Qiao, Mansour, and Laughman build a scalable system for large heating, venting, and cooling systems. Physics-guided neural differential models learn heat-swap action, tracking coolant mass and internal energy under mass and energy rules. Learned parts join algebraic solvers that enforce pressure and flow constraints, with Bayesian tuning and a lightweight fixer network trimming bias. Tests on two-compressor and scaled networks run several times faster than detailed runs with errors of only a few percent, scaling to 16 paired units.
arxiv-2604-18638: Mouslopoulos sets strict tests for a cloud of about 370 spins in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate to show time correlations that no classical model allows. Near the model's quantum critical point, two ordered phases sit in superposition, and the paper predicts a clear break of a Leggett-Garg bound on such correlations. Computer runs put the effect well within the reach of present labs, and code is supplied so others can redo the work.
arxiv-2604-19038: Wang and three colleagues factor polynomials over integer residue rings using a link to Dickson polynomials. Traditional lifting leans on Hensel's Lemma, which hides the underlying algebra. They link lifting to the roots of a special auxiliary polynomial, revealing a deterministic Dickson connection. Their Dickson-Engine algorithm runs in linear time and beats standard libraries by orders of magnitude. Applied to integers modulo 169, it builds length 182 LCD codes, near optimal against the Griesmer bound. From dimension 4, minimum distance holds at 120 even as dimension triples.
arxiv-2604-19638: Torres-Fonseca and colleagues introduce SafetyALFRED, built on the ALFRED agent benchmark and augmented with six categories of kitchen hazards. Multimodal large language models are more and more adopted as autonomous agents in interactive environments, yet they still handle safety hazards poorly. Current safety evaluations center on hazard recognition via disembodied question answering, but the authors evaluate eleven models on hazard recognition and active risk mitigation through active planning. Results reveal a significant alignment gap: models accurately spot hazards in question tests, yet average success rates remain low.
arxiv-2604-20038: Huang and four colleagues present FluSplat, a feed-forward framework for editing 3D scenes from sparse views. Past pipelines alternate 2D diffusion edits with 3D reconstruction at test time, a costly, scene-specific loop prone to cross-view mismatch. FluSplat instead enforces cross-view consistency during training with image-domain regularization and geometric alignment. Edited views then lift into 3D Gaussian Splatting in one forward pass, matching optimization methods on fidelity with far better consistency and much faster inference.
arxiv-2604-20138: Patel introduces a graph method for massless modes in latticized theory-space models, with chain models drawn from dimensional deconstruction. Fermion mass terms become bipartite graphs, with fields as vertices and mass terms as edges. The count of massless modes equals the size of a maximum matching. Their support is limited to fields reached from exposed vertices by even-length alternating paths, per the Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition. The results rest only on theory-space topology, not on model parameters, and they guide building models with chosen mode counts and localizations.
arxiv-2604-20538: Magi, Schuerger, Lauvergnat, and Agostini use exact factorization, a way to split a joint wavefunction into parts, to study photons, electrons, and nuclei interacting. They focus on strong coupling between light and molecular electron states, which creates polaritons, hybrid light-matter states. Standard dynamics methods, the usual tools of chemical physics for light-driven molecular behavior, are examined through this lens. On model studies, the team tests how well those methods perform and checks their basis for polariton systems.
arxiv-2604-20638: Sudarshan, Arora, and Chhabria offer GreenFPGA, a tool that gauges the carbon footprint of FPGAs over their life with uncertainty. Carbon footprint covers running and built-in gases from use, making, and design. FPGAs stand out through reuse, spreading built-in footprint across many uses. GreenFPGA counts footprint from design, making, reuse, use, scrap, testing, and recycling, and finds regimes where FPGAs beat ASICs, GPUs, and CPUs at equal output. Across equal-output case studies, FPGAs prove more green for often changing, diverse workloads and low-volume uses.
arxiv-2604-20838: Okada and Kasai build a quantum low-density parity-check code on a Calderbank-Shor-Steane base matrix pair of length 512. That base pair matches the SPC(3) product CSS code up to permutation, and the affine-coset description proves both Tanner graphs (3,8)-regular with girth 8. The main decoding experiment uses the lifted code with lift factor P equals 32, which has parameters [[16384,4142,18 to 32]], under the depolarizing model. Enumeration rules out nontrivial logical representatives up to weight 16 on both sides, so d_X and d_Z are at least 18.
arxiv-2604-21038: Yang and Yang study two-way feedback between the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), a planetary-scale envelope of strong and weak convection, and the mesoscale storm systems inside it. Using satellite MJO indices with a long-term tracked storm data set, they sort storms by MJO phase and probe local conditions. The MJO's shifting circulation regulates storm frequency, intensity, and organization. Meanwhile, the collective momentum and heat transport of storm groups feeds back onto the large-scale flow.
arxiv-2604-21138: Jiabao Ji and six colleagues plan for robot teams in cluttered rooms by splitting the problem into waypoints for motion and a task planner above them. A curriculum-trained method feeds motion feasibility back to the task planner, so plans respect collisions and unreachable moves. On the BoxNet3D-OBS benchmark with dense obstacles and up to nine robots, the hybrid beats motion-blind and vision-language baselines on task success.
arxiv-2604-21338: Yichun Zhao and three colleagues study how mixed-ability professional teams use information representations like PDFs, spreadsheets, and charts at work. A diary study with interviews across 23 participants from 5 teams, plus two focus groups with 7 participants from 2 more teams, maps four interrelated types of failure and workaround. Workplace stigmas and shifting social dynamics shape these patterns, pushing teams toward interdependent information work. The resulting framework aims to help design better experiences for blind, low-vision, and sighted colleagues working together.
arxiv-2604-21438: Hajime Fukushima and Tomoaki Matsumoto present SFUMATO-sharp, a GPU code for self-gravitational radiation hydrodynamics with adaptive refinement. It combines a multigrid gravity solver, M1 radiation transfer with reduced light speed, non-equilibrium reactions, thermal change, and sink particles. New reaction and thermal solvers use a linear implicit method checked against Newton-Raphson. Dust heat capacity lets dust temperature evolve without repeats. Raising the dust heat store a thousandfold speeds the solver while keeping accuracy. Multi-GPU runs scale, caveat: gravity costs grow with process count.
arxiv-2604-21638: Nganjimi and five colleagues examine dataset condensation. A small synthetic dataset tries to keep the training value of a much larger real one, a useful trick for governed fields like health care. Trajectory matching steers synthetic data from parameter changes seen in real training, but can only span a limited range. Their Bezier Trajectory Matching replaces jagged training paths with smooth quadratic curves. It matches or beats standard matching on five clinical datasets.
arxiv-2604-22038: Hua, Yun, and Pavlick define and study source-modality monitoring, the ability of multimodal models to track and share the input source of pieces of information. They evaluate how far models exploit syntactic versus semantic signals to bind words like image in a prompt to exact input parts, that is, actual images. Across experiments spanning 11 vision-language models on target-modality retrieval tasks, both syntactic and semantic signals play an important role. The latter tend to outweigh the former when modalities are highly distinct distributionally.
arxiv-2604-22138: Rodriguez-Gil and Uribe show policy gradient changes under reparameterization. They make that gap exact for scalar discount linear-quadratic control with one-hidden-layer ReLU controllers. Policy gradient on weights causes pre-scaling on gain moves, plus a squared finite-step fix and an activation error. They find step-size and startup rules ensuring controllers stay stable and converge to best gains with high odds. For a given system and cost, step-size rules imply shrinkage bounds free of network width.
arxiv-2604-22438: Gu, Du and Grundy improve language model watermarking, which traces generated content authorship. The KGW scheme is attractive but degrades badly in low-entropy code and mathematical reasoning. A crucial KGW step is random vocabulary partitioning, which adjusts token choice. The authors show the next-token distribution governs token selection changes and sets the lower bound of watermark strength. Their SSG, sort-then-split by groups, partitions the vocabulary into two logit-balanced subsets, lifting the lower bound and aiding detection. Code and mathematical reasoning tests confirm its effectiveness.
arxiv-2604-22538: Ohanyan and Sálamo Candal study optimal transport on globally hyperbolic spacetimes with Orlicz-type costs u composed with time separation. Their work covers u_p for p between zero and one, and the recent negative p case. A key notion is u-separation for measure pairs, generalizing McCann's p-separation, with strong duality for the full optimization problem. In their main results, the authors characterize timelike Ricci curvature lower bounds through convexity of relative entropy along geodesics from Orlicz-type transport, a generalization of McCann's work.
arxiv-2604-22638: Kaur and 23 colleagues probe Sagittarius A* at radio frequencies below about 5 GHz on largely unexplored sub-day timescales. Using MeerKAT, they investigate 3 GHz variability on minute scales through uv-domain point-source fitting over 8 hours. They detect flux variation over a few tens of minutes, with modulation of about 6 percent, mean flux density of about 827 milliJansky, and a spectral slope near zero. They measure the structure-function slope, with a characteristic timescale of about 120 minutes. The low-frequency study constrains the black hole's emission mechanisms.
arxiv-2604-22738: Riera, Knebe, Power, Paun, and Ussing track how the spin of dark-matter halos evolves with redshift in a suite of LCDM simulations with controlled resolution. Mean spin under the Peebles definition drifts linearly, while the Bullock definition shows a non-monotonic trend turning over at intermediate redshift. They supply closed-form fitting functions so galaxy-formation models can draw realistic spin values at any redshift.
arxiv-2604-22838: Ning and seven colleagues propose DualOpt, an optimizer that treats training from scratch and fine-tuning as different jobs instead of using one rule for both. From scratch, it applies layer-wise weight decay in real time to aid convergence and generalization. For fine-tuning, it adds weight rollback so upstream and downstream weight patterns stay consistent, limiting forgotten knowledge. Across image classification, detection, and segmentation tasks, DualOpt reaches state-of-the-art results.
arxiv-2604-23238: Hartman and three colleagues defend reasoning models against distillation theft by hiding the defense's tracks. Existing defenses shift the teacher's sampling mix, harming trace quality with flaws such as incoherence and repeat chains that foes can filter. They recast antidistillation as a max-min game with a clear detectability rule, then target thought anchors, lines that shape model output. Their method, TARS, removes redundant thought anchors that add no meaning, keeping traces legible while provably limiting detectability. Tests show it hinders student learning across scales, benchmarks, and student types.
arxiv-2604-23438: Giri and Hazra estimate how much human-caused forcing has raised the odds of extreme heat, using annual temperature maxima from a leading climate model. Their framework compares factual and counterfactual worlds through return levels, modelling spatial variation with a latent Gaussian layer and a fast approximate Bayesian method. The result is a map of posterior effects across the mainland United States, highlighting hotspots where the human contribution is credibly large.
arxiv-2604-23638: Nguyen and Aledavood ask whether people have typical days, and whether each person keeps a characteristic mix of them over time. Modelling days as sequences of routine types built from sleep, movement, and device use, they find daily life resolves into about eight types per person. Validated on sensing data from over a thousand participants, routine mixes prove stable within individuals across weeks and months, forming person-specific behavioural fingerprints.
arxiv-2604-23738: Sanders studies Schur numbers in modular form, for systems of linear equations. Schur numbers concern monochromatic solutions to equations such as x plus y equals z, and Sanders shows the modular versions depend only on how many equations there are, not on their coefficients. For a single equation he proves stronger bounds.
arxiv-2604-23938: Zheng and seven colleagues present TSAssistant, a human-guided multi-agent framework that automates safety assessment reports. Research agents ground and cite one domain each, drawing on genetic, transcriptomic, homology, drug, and clinical data, while synthesis agents join findings across domains. Code hooks and steady memory enforce hard constraints, and an interactive review loop lets experts check and revise sections with full context kept. Report quality splits into reproducibility, grounding, accuracy, and control, with high reproducibility and grounding, strong match with the human report, and net-positive expert review.
arxiv-2604-24038: Gao, Wang, and Yu introduce AgentPulse, a live evaluation framework that scores 50 agents across 10 workload types. Four factors, benchmark results, adoption signals, community feeling, and ecosystem health, draw on 18 real-time signals from code hosts, registries, marketplaces, social sites, and leaderboards. A test free of code-host signals still predicts outside adoption measures, while benchmark-only and full rankings nearly disagree on a small subset. The authors stress it is a method for surfacing deployment signals, not a final ranking.
arxiv-2604-24138: Yasuda and five colleagues propose synchronized molecular dynamics for thin-layer flows of complex fluids. Thin layers split into cross-sectional motion shaped by interfaces and streamwise transport along the channel. The method scatters local molecular cells along the channel and syncs them through macroscopic conservation laws, updating cell forces so velocity profiles and pressure emerge without preset constitutive rules. Tests on Lennard-Jones wedge flows match a slip-aware Reynolds equation, and polymer lubrication runs capture shear-thinning with microscopic chain motion.
arxiv-2604-24638: Barrionuevo, Tirao and Vera construct families of k-step nilpotent symplectic Lie algebras associated with graphs, extending a construction for the two-step case. Graphs give a concrete way to build these algebras, one graph at a time. A nilpotent Lie algebra is one where repeated brackets eventually vanish, and k marks how many steps that takes. Under mild conditions on the nilpotency type, they also show that symplectic Lie algebras of that type exist. The existence result says such algebras are not rare special cases.
arxiv-2604-24938: Kim and five colleagues study depth pruning in large language models from a functional view. Depth pruning improves run speed by removing Transformer blocks. Evaluating typical model families across diverse calibration setups and multiple search methods, they show different setups produce different pruned sets. Under a fixed calibration setup, complex search methods yield only small gains over simple one-shot methods, landing on similar pruned sets. Overall, calibration setup matters far more than search method choice for pruning patterns and calibration scores, and mattering comparably for downstream reasoning score spread.
arxiv-2604-25038: Doran and three colleagues develop equation learning for multiscale TB models. Tuberculosis probably replaced COVID-19 as the leading infectious cause of death globally in 2023. Over 10 million people are found yearly, with most adult cases in males, at 62.5 percent. Male excess burden likely reflects within-host factors and population factors. The authors build a sex-split framework, learning equations for average within-host model output. Population numbers evolve between hosts via equations, linked by stochastic links. Counterfactual cases probe sex and gender effects on disease spread.
arxiv-2604-25238: Ballico and Gasparim prove that the subset of irregular bundles is meager within a moduli space of stable bundles on a Hopf surface. The space covers bundles of rank r and second Chern class c greater than zero. In the paper's notation, this moduli space is written M with subscripts r and c. Meager here means small in the topological sense, a countable union of nowhere dense sets.
arxiv-2604-25338: Baik and four colleagues put forth RecFlash, a fast recommender speed-up that remaps data for NAND flash in-storage computing. Recommender systems are widely used, but fast-growing user data makes live handling hard. Flash in-storage computing holds huge user data well. Unlike other neural uses, recommenders show spotty, random memory reads. Most data pulled to the page buffer goes unused, wasting bandwidth and slowing inference. RecFlash cuts latency and power use by up to 81 percent and 91.9 percent over past in-storage computing.
arxiv-2604-25538: The CMS team measures 25 jet substructure observables at once in large-radius jets with high transverse momentum from proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. The measurement covers dijet events and top-antitop events rich in boosted W bosons and top quarks, with jets of one, two, or three prongs. Data span 138 inverse femtobarns recorded by CMS in 2016 to 2018. A six-body basis of N-subjettiness observables overconstrains the phase space of emissions. Results are unfolded to stable-particle level, so the set can test and refine models of radiation in jets.
arxiv-2604-25838: Kumar and five colleagues analyze quarkonium polarization in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider with PYTHIA8. It probes how charm and bottom bound states form, read through muon angles from their decays. The team computes momentum spectra at forward rapidity for charmonia and bottomonia at 7 and 13 TeV. Detector flaws and muon smearing are added to mimic real conditions, since they can fake the signal. Results are checked against recent ALICE measurements.
arxiv-2604-26238: Song and seven colleagues developed EnerGS, a scene-reconstruction method that treats partial geometric evidence as a soft guide rather than a hard rule. Laser-scan priors are often patchy outdoors, so the method models them as a continuous energy field steering Gaussian primitives without boxing in the solution. On large outdoor scenes, it improved image quality and geometric stability under sparse and single-view settings while curbing overfitting.
arxiv-2604-26538: Chaturvedi and Nath studied round cosmic string loops in a flat expanding universe with a fractional Polyakov setup that remembers the past. Letting loop size and polar angle change together gives a linked system driven by string tension, expansion, and a spin-out term. Unlike standard collapse stories, some solutions grow steadily, powered by self-made angular motion. The system also shows twisty behavior with chaos marks, whose start tracks growing solutions closely.
arxiv-2604-26638: Ye, Chen, and Yin show how pi emerges from equatorial localization on the sphere, by a non-radial quantum route. For the top-weight branch of spherical harmonics, a rigidity index captures the localization, and its value at finite quantum number is a Wallis partial product. The mechanism works for the rigid rotor and for the surface of a thin spherical shell, where frozen radial motion leaves only the angular problem. At large quantum numbers, the probability cloud gathers near the equator and the Wallis formula returns.
arxiv-2604-26738: Kim and Lee propose MulViT-TF, a vision-only method for estimating signal strength from multi-view observations. Standard feedback estimation adds uplink overhead, suffers unstable measurements, and lags behind feedback loops. That lag blocks fast adaptation, while vision methods lack spatial diversity for camera-side blocked-view cases. Transformer fusion of multi-view observations gives wider coverage with no extra sensing inputs. In two indoor scenes, it cuts error by over a quarter and lifts 3dB error coverage by nearly 14 points over the best single-view rival.
arxiv-2604-26838: Ene and three colleagues build differentially private solvers for positive linear programs, covering packing, covering, and mixed forms. They work in the high-sensitivity constraint-private regime, where near instances differ by one free constraint and no solver can meet each constraint. Their solvers return near solutions while breaking only a set number of constraints, beating past instance-dependent bounds and adding new bounds that hinge only on size. The method builds on dense multiplicative weights from a regularized dual view.
arxiv-2604-27038: Salazar studies phase changes on triadic hypergraphs, where a formation field evolves under Ginzburg-Landau flow with a cubic coupling, while views swap by Kawasaki exchange. Near the critical point the cubic coupling is minor and the change stays continuous, led by an Ising base with tuned coupling. The triadic correlator, one over an order value, has exponents beta-TF 3/2 and gamma-TF minus 1. Its susceptibility goes to zero at that temperature instead of blowing up. Adding back coupling makes it first-order, with an endpoint at zero coupling.
arxiv-2604-27438: Jazlan and three colleagues systematically measure web tracking on 20 AI chatbots, using a sensitive prompt in ordinary chats and, where offered, private chats. They check content exposure, including prompts, titles, links, and identifiers, and identity exposure, including names, emails, identifiers, cookies, and network fields. They find 17 of the 20 chatbots pass information to at least one outside party. Three share plain conversation text with Microsoft Clarity through replay. Fifteen share links or identifiers with advertising, analytics, or social endpoints, and several expose identity through widgets and replay tags, including hashed emails.
arxiv-2604-27538: Moummad and five colleagues study self-supervised learning for plant image recognition, a field key to biodiversity monitoring. They show that common augmentations such as blur, grayscale conversion, and solarization harm plant images by erasing fine cues needed to tell species apart. Affine transforms and posterization work better, and training SimDINOv2 on an iNaturalist 2021 Plantae slice beats training on ImageNet-1K. Their models match or beat strong supervised baselines on few-shot plant tasks.
arxiv-2604-27638: Bradley and Cross compare black-box and grey-box machine learning models for structural health monitoring through a green lens. Purely data-driven models falter where data from relevant environmental and operating conditions are missing, while grey-box models add an engineer's physical insight about the structure. The authors test whether the strong extrapolation of grey-box models cuts runtimes and thus carbon emissions. They aim for physics-informed models with lower computational cost that keep high performance, shown in a structural health monitoring case study.
arxiv-2604-27738: Białas and four colleagues propose a transformer sampler for two-dimensional spin systems that generates groups of spins per step instead of one. They also build an approximated-probability model, further improving efficiency. Despite heavier computation than dense or convolutional networks, their sampler handles systems up to 180 by 180 spins for the Ising model. Its effective sample size is about 20 times the previous best neural sampler's on the 128 by 128 Ising model at critical temperature. They also test the method on the two-dimensional Edwards-Anderson model with 64 by 64 spin systems.
arxiv-2605-00138: Kirill Shakhmatov proves a single clean statement linking cylinders and an ideal. Given an additive group action on an affine variety, one can gather all the principal invariant cylinders inside it. Shakhmatov shows that whatever lies outside the union of those cylinders is exactly the zero locus of the plinth ideal of the corresponding locally nilpotent derivation. The result equates a geometric complement on one side with an algebraic vanishing set on the other.
arxiv-2605-00238:
Longwei Cong and 5 co-authors bring a tool from education research, item response theory, to the grading of short student answers by language models. Usual scores such as F1 hide where a grader struggles. Their framework instead models each grade as a contest between the grader's ability and the answer's difficulty.

Applied to seventeen open-weight models on two benchmarks, the method shows that models with alike overall scores can fade at very different rates as answers get harder. Errors on hard answers pile up on one middle label, for partly correct but incomplete work. Hard answers also tend to match the reference answer weakly and sit far from other answers in meaning.
arxiv-2605-00338:
Yi Xiao and 5 co-authors report a new behavior in cavity optomechanical systems, where light trapped in a cavity pushes on a tiny mechanical resonator. Such systems are known for oscillation, chaos, and amplitude locking under different drives. The team studies a system whose built-in mechanical frequency is neither very large nor very small, driven by a two-tone field.

When the gap between the two tones matches the mechanical frequency, the resonator's energy climbs in a staircase pattern, step by step. The authors map how the pattern changes with device parameters and drive conditions, including uneven tone powers and small mismatches. Some features, such as a sudden split caused by uneven powers, appear only in this middle frequency class. Possible uses include phonon lasers and precision sensing.
arxiv-2605-00438:
Jinkun Liu and 8 co-authors teach robot policies to think in text and images at once. Long manipulation tasks need plans that are logically sound and geometrically grounded. Text-only reasoning orders the steps but misses spatial limits, while image prediction shows geometry but stays local and vague. Latent plans, hidden inside the network, cannot be inspected at all.

Their framework builds an explicit trace that alternates written subgoals with visual keyframes across the whole task. One multimodal model generates the trace from the opening view and the instruction, caches it, and a closed-loop controller then acts under its guidance. Training traces are manufactured by slicing demonstrations into stages and captioning each stage automatically. On long-horizon simulation benchmarks the interleaved trace far outperformed text-only, image-only, and no-trace variants, though the authors note stale or wrong global plans remain a weakness.
arxiv-2605-00638:
Zichun Ye and 5 co-authors open the study of machine unlearning for sequential decision-making, starting with offline stochastic multi-armed bandits. Unlearning answers data-deletion requests by removing a point's influence from a trained model without full retraining. It has been studied for supervised and unsupervised learning. Bandits, where a policy was learned from logged choices among arms, pose fresh privacy questions. This paper formalizes them for the first time.

The authors measure utility by post-unlearning decision quality, and study single-source and multi-source deletion under two data-generation models. Their algorithms build on two canonical tools, a Gaussian mechanism and rollback, switching adaptively between them by data regime and privacy demand. Performance guarantees and matching lower bounds are proved across the settings. Experiments confirm the predicted trade-offs.
arxiv-2605-00838:
Ayon Roy, Sadman Sharif, and Shiva Prasad Sarkar build a learning system that sets alarm thresholds for 4G mobile networks automatically. Alarms warn when a cell shuts down or behaves abnormally, and fixed manual thresholds can miss serious faults at busy times or trigger needless callouts when the network is quiet. Their framework predicts four thresholds from live network behavior, including audit window and fluctuation limits.

Because no true labels exist, thresholds are derived by a percentile-guided strategy. On anonymized data from more than ten thousand cells, their PCTN model beats a boosted-tree baseline, a CNN-BiLSTM, and an iTransformer on most targets while using far fewer parameters than the transformer. Outputs stay interpretable, and daily retraining keeps thresholds current.
arxiv-2605-01238:
Zikang Leng and five co-authors release EduGage, a multimodal dataset and benchmark for estimating learner engagement during self-guided video learning from sensor signals. Engagement spans attentional, emotional, and cognitive dimensions, and measuring it can support learners and adaptive systems. Wearable and camera sensors record physiological and motion signals including heart, brain, skin, and eye-tracking measures during a study with a small group of participants.

Participants completed learning tasks and gave repeated in-situ ratings of how hard it was to pay attention during the preceding minute. A modality-aware reference model outperforms sensor-free, statistical, deep, foundation-model, and language-model baselines on several metrics. Fine-grained estimation proves feasible but inherently noisy, and the preferred sensing setup depends on the target metric and practical burden.
arxiv-2605-01438:
Hyunho Cha and Jungwoo Lee refine direct fidelity estimation, a way to grade how close a lab-made quantum state sits to a target state without full tomography. A prior method tunes measurements to the target but settles for a stand-in objective rather than the true worst-case spread.

The pair replace that stand-in with an exact spectral form that works for any target state. They pin down all fair linear estimators with one operator identity. They also find the best sampling rule for fixed rebuild weights. Then they turn the worst-case design problem into a semidefinite program that a computer can solve. The recipe is run with local Pauli measurements, the lab staple. In noisy simulations, the exact design beats the older surrogate on estimation spread, which means fewer shots for the same trust in the grade.
arxiv-2605-01538:
Paul Xing and six co-authors correct the blur that the skull imposes on ultrasound images of the brain. Sound bent by bone misplaces the tiny bubbles used as tracers. That dulls the super-resolution maps and spawns fake vessels, a standing block for imaging through the skull in animals and, one day, patients.

Their method builds beamforming, the focusing step, in a differentiable form, so an optimizer can tune a spatial map of the aberration automatically. The tuning target is angular coherence, a measure of how well views agree. In living mice and nonhuman primates, the corrected images sharpen, and functional ultrasound gains sensitivity as well. A three-dimensional version clears duplicated vessels in primate brains. The authors present the fully automatic fix as a way to spread skull-through imaging across labs and species.
arxiv-2605-01938:
Mahmoud Ahmed and colleagues measure energy use during multimodal training on NVIDIA Grace Hopper superchips. Models that learn from text, images, and video at once grow fast, and moving data can cost more than computing. Tools such as DeepSpeed ease the load by offloading and checkpointing, but those fixes add activity of their own.

Grace Hopper chips link CPU and GPU closely, with shared memory and a fast interconnect. The authors trace how application, runtime, and hardware layers interact on this system. Their analysis shows where the fast link lowers transfer cost and where training choices still waste energy, giving a fuller picture than speed alone.
arxiv-2605-02038:
Ranit Karmakar and Jayita Chatterjee audit language models by varying the prompt, rather than trusting a single prompt score. They study fifteen open-weight models, focusing on ten instruction models across five classification and reasoning tests, each under five prompt variants. For every case they record accuracy, two forms of calibration, parse rate, and spread across prompts.

Evaluation choices alone changed conclusions a lot. One definition change shifted calibration by a large mean amount. Pairing a chain-of-thought prompt with a first-character scorer cut apparent accuracy sharply on one test, and repair steps recovered most of the loss. The audit shows single-prompt accuracy misses reliability failures that matter in practice.
arxiv-2605-02538:
Ali Askari and Jens Gerken write a position paper on social robot touch: handshakes, a reassuring stroke, and other contact meant to carry feeling. Robots have grown better at gripping and handling objects using touch data, yet warm, social touch remains hard. The gap is sometimes called a haptic uncanny valley, where near-human touch feels wrong.

Drawing on neurobiology, the authors split affective touch into distinct sub-tasks, each handled by a specialized model. The models share state in a peer-to-peer, closed-loop design, rather than acting as one large motor program. That split should let specialists in haptics, AI, and robotics each improve their part within a shared simulation-to-real path. The goal is a unified system for expressive social robots.
arxiv-2605-02638:
Jiawei Ge and eleven co-authors tackle tracking several objects, named in plain language, across multiple camera views. Keeping one identity for the same object in every view normally requires costly frame-level labels. The team explores a weakly supervised version that uses only object category labels, leaning on large foundation models for help.

Direct use of those models failed: they misread referring phrases and lost identities across views, though their tracklets were reliable. So the models serve as pseudo-label generators. A first stage refines and links their tracklets across cameras, and a second stage trains the authors' ViewSAM model on those labels. The design aims to cut annotation cost while keeping cross-view tracking accurate, a need in surveillance and sports analysis.
arxiv-2605-03038:
Anna M. Staśto, Himanshu Raj, and Raju Venugopalan recast gluon and graviton radiation in strong-field shockwave collisions as squeezed states. Radiation in this regime is described by Lipatov vertices, and the graviton vertex is a bilinear copy of the gluon one, a link called the double copy.

They show the multi-gluon spectrum forms a generalized squeezed coherent state and argue the same holds for gravitons. Large squeezing values are feasible for near-minimal uncertainty states. That boosts quantum noise in the gravitational wave spectrum above the reach of current and future detectors, a strong motive for fuller study.
arxiv-2605-03438:
Zihao Guo, Yiding Sun, Jihua Zhu, Haozhe Cheng, Jian Liu, and Ajmal Saeed Mian present Mantis, a tuning method for 3D point cloud foundation models built on Mamba backbones. Full fine-tuning is costly, and existing light tuning tools were designed for transformers, clashing with Mamba's state-level dynamics and degrading accuracy.

A state-aware adapter injects small task signals directly into the selective state updates while the backbone stays frozen. A consistency distillation step also steadies the model across different point orderings. Across benchmarks, Mantis stayed competitive while training under five percent of backbone parameters, the first Mamba-native solution of its kind.
arxiv-2605-03538:
Konstantinos D. Katsanos, Panagiotis Gavriilidis, and George C. Alexandropoulos design robust distributed beamforming for cell-free systems with dynamic metasurface antennas. Metasurfaces promise huge arrays at lower power and cost. But central optimization needs heavy processing and perfect channel knowledge.

Their framework splits analog and digital beamforming across stations, with minimal control exchange. It uses a realistic element model and imperfect channel data. A parallel split configures each station's tunable elements to maximize spectral efficiency. Tests confirm robustness across channel conditions. They also show mutual coupling must be modeled during design. The design keeps each station's load low while the whole system stays in tune.
arxiv-2605-04538:
Priyanshi Bhasin, Diptiman Sen, and Tanmoy Das develop the basic theory of anyons. These exotic particles have exchange behaviour between that of ordinary particle types. They are of interest for quantum information. A consistent framework must handle both their local occupancy limits and the phases they pick up when swapped.

For a one-dimensional family of abelian anyons, the authors build an algebra that caps how many can share a site while keeping the right exchange phase between sites. They also prove an exact duality linking one anyon case to spin-one particles. It turns an anyon hopping model into a spin model. That model has density-dependent flux and both gapped and gapless regions.
arxiv-2605-04738:
